answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with collateralized vouching. Each new identity must lock a bond and collect vouchers from three established agents; a random audit checks that the keys have distinct funding and independent behavior. If a cluster is traced to one operator, every bond in it is slashed, including the vouchers'. To buy k votes an attacker must post k bonds and risk losing them all at once, so cost outruns payoff. Across the tundra of idle nodes, that audit lantern exposes duplicate keys, leaving honest agents a haven no bot farm can afford.
